overview:
The Arvada Police Department utilizes Flock Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) cameras to support criminal investigations and enhance community safety. These stationary cameras only capture still images of license plates as well as key vehicle characteristics, including color, make, and unique identifying features such as bumper/window stickers, top/back racks, or tool boxes. This information is often crucial when suspects remove or alter license plates to avoid detection. By allowing investigators to search for distinctive vehicle traits, ALPR technology helps us more efficiently identify suspects, recover stolen vehicles, and solve crimes, often without escalating encounters or putting the public at additional risk.


The Arvada Police Department is committed to protecting individual privacy and ensuring all technology is used lawfully and responsibly. Our ALPR practices operate within clear constitutional boundaries and are guided by long-standing principles of public safety, accountability, and transparency. In accordance with department policy, all Flock data and images are automatically deleted after 30 days, unless they are preserved as evidence in an active investigation. This limited retention period ensures an appropriate balance between investigative effectiveness and privacy protections.

more_info.Recent Success Stories:
The summaries below provide real examples of how ALPR data has contributed to arrests, vehicle recoveries and investigative breakthroughs, including violent crime cases. These examples also demonstrate how the system is used responsibly, including instances where alerts helped exonerate someone and prevent unnecessary enforcement action.


Cases are listed in chronological order, beginning with the most recent.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR26002067 | Jan. 28, 2026 | Suspicious Incident

Police received a report that an individual was seen dragging what appeared to be a person into a minivan. Officers responded but were unable to locate the vehicle. During an area canvass, investigators obtained surveillance video showing a white male exiting a gray minivan on West 57th Avenue. The male placed a backpack on a bench inside Wolff Park, returned to the vehicle, then appeared to drag an unconscious or possibly deceased person to the rear and opposite side of the minivan before placing the individual back inside and driving westbound.

Based on the video, the situation appeared extremely concerning and potentially involved a homicide. Investigators searched Flock ALPR cameras in the area and located the minivan. Using the captured license plate, officers contacted the registered owner and determined the driver had picked up a family member experiencing substance abuse issues and initially wanted to drop him in the park to sleep. The driver then became concerned and transported the family member to a hospital for medical attention, which investigators confirmed with hospital staff.

Impact: ALPR technology allowed investigators to quickly identify the vehicle and determine that no crime had occurred. Without ALPR data, the incident could have remained an active and resource-intensive investigation involving a suspected body disposal.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR2600018 | Jan. 1, 2026 | Auto Theft


A Flock alert identified a stolen vehicle at Home Depot. The vehicle was later located near Harkins Theatre, and the suspect was taken into custody.


Impact: ALPR provided real-time location information that led to rapid recovery of the vehicle and the arrest of the suspect.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25022781 | Dec. 26, 2025 | Recovered Stolen Vehicle


A Flock alert notified officers that a stolen vehicle was in the area. When officers attempted contact, the suspects fled and crashed before fleeing on foot. Evidence was recovered from the scene, and the investigation continued.


Impact: ALPR allowed officers to quickly locate a stolen vehicle, resulting in recovery and additional investigative evidence.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25022515 | Dec. 21, 2025 | Felony Menacing


An ALPR camera alerted officers to a vehicle connected to a hit-and-run investigation. Officers attempted contact with the suspect, who produced an edged weapon and barricaded himself inside the van. After negotiations, the suspect surrendered and was jailed on felony menacing and related charges.


Impact: ALPR helped officers locate a suspect and resolve a dangerous situation safely.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25017866 | Oct. 11, 2025 | Carjacking / Attempted Homicide


After a shooting, suspects stole the victim’s vehicle. The Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office monitored Flock alerts and was notified when the vehicle passed a camera. Deputies located and pursued the vehicle, ultimately arresting both suspects.


Impact: Regional ALPR collaboration enabled rapid cross-jurisdictional identification and arrest in a violent felony case.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25017405 | Oct. 4, 2025 | Attempted Murder


Detectives investigated a shooting involving two vehicles. Through interviews, one vehicle was determined to be uninvolved. The suspect vehicle was identified using ALPR data. Investigators noted that the ALPR identification was the first critical lead in the case. Without it, the investigation likely would have stalled. The identification ultimately led to the arrest of the shooter.


Impact: ALPR served as the key investigative breakthrough that led to a successful arrest in a shooting case.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25008595 | May 22, 2025 | Vehicular Assault


A teenage couple became involved in an argument. During the incident, the female jumped onto the hood of a white Chevrolet, fell off and was run over, sustaining serious injuries including a broken pelvis. The driver fled. Officers used Flock cameras in the area to identify the vehicle and obtain a license plate number. That information allowed investigators to locate and later charge the driver.


Impact: ALPR data quickly identified a fleeing vehicle in a serious injury case, resulting in the arrest of a suspect.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25007636 | May 8, 2025 | Fatal Hit-and-Run


A person using a personal mobility chair was struck and killed by a pickup truck whose driver fled the scene. Investigators searched nearby Flock cameras and quickly identified a possible suspect vehicle and license plate. Additional ALPR data helped investigators determine it was not with the registered owner, leading to identification and arrest of the suspect.


Impact: ALPR provided critical early leads in a fatal crash investigation, accelerating suspect identification.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25022885 | April 28, 2025 | Auto Theft (Exclusionary Use)


A Flock alert indicated a stolen vehicle at Home Depot. Officers contacted the driver inside the store. The investigation revealed the driver had permission to possess the vehicle and that the stolen entry from another jurisdiction was incorrect. The alert allowed officers to safely resolve the issue without incident.


Impact: ALPR enabled officers to clear a records error and prevent unnecessary escalation.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25007074 | April 28, 2025 | Auto Theft (Exclusionary Use)


A Flock alert identified a stolen work van traveling on Ralston Road. Before initiating a stop, officers contacted the registered owner, who confirmed he was driving the vehicle and had mistakenly reported it stolen.


Impact: ALPR allowed officers to verify information before taking enforcement action, preventing an unnecessary stop.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25006276 | April 15, 2025 | Auto Theft / Felony Menacing


An officer received a Flock alert while patrolling for a stolen vehicle. The vehicle was found occupied at an apartment complex. The female driver was arrested for First-Degree Motor Vehicle Theft. A second stolen vehicle parked next to it was also recovered. Evidence related to a felony menacing case involving a firearm from the previous night was recovered from one of the vehicles.


Impact: One ALPR alert led to two stolen vehicle recoveries, an arrest and evidence recovery tied to a violent crime.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25004818 | March 22, 2025 | Felony Warrants


An ALPR alert identified a stolen license plate. Officers located the vehicle and contacted the occupants. Both were arrested on outstanding felony warrants.


Impact: ALPR facilitated the safe apprehension of wanted individuals.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25002192 | Feb. 7, 2025 | Auto Theft


An ALPR alert identified a stolen vehicle. The suspect was located and charged with motor vehicle theft and drug possession.


Impact: ALPR supported vehicle recovery and the arrest of the suspect.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR25000692 | Jan. 13, 2025 | Armed Carjacking (Juvenile Suspects)


Juveniles pistol-whipped a driver at a Lakewood gas station and stole his Jeep at gunpoint. Shortly after, a Flock camera later detected the stolen Jeep in Arvada. Officers located the vehicle, and after a brief pursuit, safely stopped it. Three juvenile suspects were taken into custody. A .40-caliber Glock handgun equipped with an illegal auto switch was recovered. Two suspects were linked to additional auto theft investigations.


Impact: ALPR detection enabled rapid identification and safe apprehension of armed carjacking suspects.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR24018646 | Nov. 1, 2024 | Auto Theft


An ALPR alert identified a stolen vehicle. Contact with the occupants resulted in one arrest for motor vehicle theft and another arrest on outstanding warrants.


Impact: ALPR contributed to stolen vehicle recovery and the arrest of wanted individuals.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR24015422 | Sept. 8, 2024 | Vehicular Assault


Following a vehicle sale dispute, a suspect intentionally struck a motorcyclist. Investigators searched ALPR cameras for a matching vehicle description. The search identified the suspect vehicle, including matching damage. Later that day, another agency recovered the vehicle, and the driver was arrested.


Impact: ALPR provided rapid suspect vehicle identification in an intentional assault case.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AR23012579 | Aug. 8, 2023 | At-Risk Adult / Cybercrime Investigation


An ALPR alert identified a vehicle connected to an active investigation involving theft from an at-risk adult, identity theft and a theft series. Officers contacted the suspects based on the alert, and charges were filed.


Impact: ALPR helped investigators locate suspects involved in financial exploitation of a vulnerable community member.
more_info.Arvada Police Department ALPR Policy: The Arvada Police Department's ALPR policy (Policy Manual 460) is available for public review on our website (https://public.powerdms.com/APD10/documents/819542). The policy outlines how ALPR data is collected, accessed, used, and retained. The Arvada Police Department remains dedicated to transparency, responsible technology use, and safeguarding the trust of the community we serve.
